2. The case, of the plaintiffs, inter alia. was that Jinnat AIi, predecessor of the plaintiff- respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and others was 16 annas owner of suit property No. 1 measuring 1.46 acres recorded in CS Khatian No. 236 and owner of 15 gondas share of suit property No .2 recorded in CS Khatian No. 233; that the said Jinnat Ali died leaving 3 sons named Abdul Haque, Dr. Fazler Rahman and Dudu Miah and one daughter Kulsumernessa; that Dudu Mia became traceless before his death; that Abdul Haque died leaving plaintiff No.1 and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as 3 sons and plaintiff No. 2 and defendant Nos. 3 and 4 as three daughters and defendant No. 5 as his widow; that the plaintiffs became owners of 1 annas 17 gondas 1 kara and 1 kranti share in the properties of Jinnat Ali; that defendant Nos. 6-9 are the heirs of Fazler Rahman and Kulsamernessa; that defendant Nos. 10-20 are heirs of Khalil Patwari owner of Property No. 2 and other defendants are purchasers from the co-sharers; that there was no partition and the defendants having refused to amicably partition the land the plaintiffs filed the suit for partition. 

 3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 10, 11, 13-15 contending inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no title and possession; that the suit for simple partition is not maintainable; that the suit property Nos. 1 and 2 originally belonged to Sadaruddin, father of Khalil Patwari and Jinnat Ali on the basis of kabuliyat dated 8th Jaistha 1288 BS; that the landlord auction sold the said holding for arrears of rent in Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905 and one Kalimuddin auction purchased the same and got delivery of possession through Court; that thereafter he sold the same to Khalil Patwari by kabala dated 17th Kartick 1312 BS; that thereafter the said Jinnat Ali took settlement of 12 gondas equivalent to '72 acres from Khalil Patwari by executing Kabuliyat dated 27th Ashar. 1320 BS; that the said properties of Jinnat Ali were subsequently auction purchased by the heirs of Khalil Patwari for arrears of rent and possessed the same by taking delivery of possession through Court; that thereafter the landlord auction purchased the entire lands of the said original jote in Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 for arrears of rent impleading all the heirs of Khalil Patwari and Jinnat Ali; and the landlord took delivery of possession in the said property through Court; that thereafter the answering defendants. plaintiffs brother defendant No. 1 and Fazler Rahman predecessor of defendant Nos. 6-8 took fresh settlement from the auction purchaser landlord; that defendant No. 1 and Fazler Rahman took settlement of specified '86 acres of lands; that the plaintiffs have been residing in the settled lands of defendant No.1 and Fazler Rahman; that Jinnat Ali was never owner in the properties of Khatian No. 233 and the same belonged to Khalil Patwari; that Jinnat Ali was owner of '72 acres in the properties of Khatian No. 236 but he fraudulently recorded his name in Khatian No. 233 as 15 gondas owner and recorded more lands in excess of his '72 acres in under raiyati khatian No. 236; that both the khatians are wrong and that the plaintiffs are not owners of '24 acres as claimed by them. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The lower appellate Court reversed the judgment of the trial Court after holding that on the face of CS Khatian Ext. 1 and 1 (a) finally published between 1913-16, bearing the name of Jinnat Ali, as the owner of the suit land, the alleged auction sale of the same in Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905 and the exhibits in support thereof are of no relevance and only indicate at its best that the alleged sale was a paper transaction. The lower appellate Court further held that even if there was any auction sale in paper the owners of the properties did not part with their possession and they actually possessed during the last CS operation and that the defendants having failed to produce any writ of delivery of possession about their alleged Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 the interest of Jinnat Ali was not extinguished and Jinnat Ali had subsisting interest in the disputed property and consequently decreed the suit. The lower appellate Court accepted the correctness of the CS khatian and their presumptive value on the face of the documentary evidences adduced by the defendants to prove the auction sale and subsequent delivery of possession.
